source.title: Turning the Spell Around: Lightweight Alignment Amplification via Rank-One Safety Injection
source.authors: H. Shairah; Hasan Abed Al Kader Hammoud; G. Turkiyyah; Bernard Ghanem

record.file_problem: None; the full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: The paper tests whether benign instruction fine-tuning changes harmful-request refusal, using a different fine-tuning setup and reporting harmful refusal rates. Its layer-injection ablation also bears on whether safety can be localized to a small subset of layers.
record.gate_note: The paper's ROSI and jailbreak results generally measure safety amplification or attack robustness, not the specified fine-tuning, response-token-position, compliant-prefill, suffix, decoding, or safety-depth claims. The layer-injection ablation is retained for V5. Table 7 is retained for V2. Generic jailbreak benchmark scores are not assigned to V4 because the tested attack mechanisms are not specified as the mechanisms named in that version. Cited findings from other work are excluded.
record.test_reason: Appendix A fine-tunes Llama-2-7B-Chat with LoRA on benign Dolly-15k and reports harm refusal before (99.8%) and after (82.7%). That bears on V2. The rest of the paper evaluates the authors' ROSI steering edit, which is a mitigation, not a test of any version.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors conclude ROSI raises refusal and jailbreak robustness in aligned models and restores refusal in uncensored models with little utility loss. They note a safety system prompt is needed to extract the vector from uncensored models. In Appendix A, benign LoRA fine-tuning lowered HR to 82.7%. ROSI applied after fine-tuning gave only marginal recovery (85.5%), while ROSI before fine-tuning kept 98.6%, and ROSI→SafeLoRA reached 100%.
record.recipe_differences: For the benign-fine-tuning result, the study uses LoRA on DATABRICKS DOLLY 15K for 3000 steps and measures HR on Llama-2-7B-Chat; it also tests ROSI and SAFE LORA sequences. This is a single-model, limited configuration rather than a broad reproduction.
record.method_sensitivity: Fine-tuning sequence changes the outcome: ROSI before LoRA retains 98.6% HR, while LoRA before ROSI yields 85.5%. The layer-ablation results also vary with the number and identity of injected layers.

fits_no_version.finding: A rank-one weight edit along a difference-in-means refusal direction raises harm refusal across 9 aligned models and re-adds refusal to uncensored Dolphin models. Effect saturates when injected into about 30–40% of layers, with large variance by layer choice.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Refusal can be amplified or restored by a rank-one steering edit along a single activation direction; efficacy depends on how many and which layers are edited.

fits_no_version.finding: Injecting ROSI before LoRA fine-tuning keeps HR at 98.6%, versus 82.7% for LoRA alone; applying ROSI after LoRA recovers only to 85.5%.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Pre-fine-tuning safety-direction injection mitigates benign fine-tuning erosion better than post-hoc repair (mitigation result).

record.peer_reviewed: Proceedings of the 2026 Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing
record.problems: The fine-tuning experiment reports HR for only one model and one instruction-tuning dataset/configuration, with no uncertainty estimate stated for Table 7. Layer-ablation values are presented graphically; the text provides only qualitative trends and a single-run 100% result.
record.rows_left_out: No rows from the main ROSI safety, jailbreak, or utility tables were included because those results do not test the specified versions directly. Generic jailbreak benchmark results do not identify whether compliant prefills, suffixes, or decoding changes were used. Cited results from prior studies are excluded.

untested.parts: Only one model (Llama-2-7B-Chat), one benign dataset (Dolly), one configuration (3000 steps, LoRA rank 32). No full fine-tuning, no few-example or carefully chosen benign data, no other models, no uncertainty.
No harmful-data fine-tuning. Dolphin models are pre-uncensored, and no before/after values are given.
Not tested. Jailbreak benchmarks are aggregate and do not isolate prefilling, suffix or decoding attacks.
Not tested. Layer ablations concern where an added steering edit acts, not where existing safety lives.

record.verdict_notes: Only Appendix A Table 7's LoRA row bears on a version (V2), and only as the baseline for the authors' defense. The reader's V2 limits_scope label was built on defense-method rows, which do not qualify V2, so it is removed. The V5 label is removed: the layer ablations test the study's own steering injection, not localization of existing safety. The record's peer_reviewed field (EMNLP 2026) is not supported by the provided text, which shows only an arXiv header.

versions.untested_parts: The paper does not fine-tune on harmful examples to measure whether they remove refusal.
Tests one model and one instruction-tuning dataset/configuration; it does not test fine-tuning on a few to a few hundred examples.
Does not isolate compliant-opening prefills, adversarial suffixes, or decoding changes.

The layer ablation varies which and how many layers receive ROSI; it does not establish localization to a small set of individual weights or test whether safety behavior itself is carried by a small set of ranks.
Does not test why safety would be shallow in response-token positions.
Does not train or evaluate safety spread beyond initial response tokens.

relationships.condition: Llama-2-7B-Chat, standard LoRA on Dolly-15k, 3000 steps, HR on CatQA judged by LlamaGuard 3
relationships.reason: Harm refusal fell from 99.8% to 82.7% after benign LoRA fine-tuning (R1, R2). Single run, no uncertainty reported.
relationships.display_finding: Harm refusal fell from 99.8% to 82.7% in a single run with no reported uncertainty.
